author: TEDx Talks
description:
There are an estimated 28 million people living in modern slavery today. Many of them made something you're holding right now. Dr. Bonnie Nixon’s work explores the intersection
of environmental justice and modern slavery, highlighting how consumer goods like your smartphone are manufactured through complex global networks.

The question Dr. Nixon has spent her career asking — and answering — is the one most of us avoid: if slavery was never abolished but simply outsourced, what does that make the rest of us? Unwitting participants, perhaps. But participants who still have a choice.

#ForcedLabor #EnvironmentalJustice #CorporateAccountability #EthicalTech #ModernSlavery #SupplyChainEthics #HumanRights #ConsumerResponsibility

What You'll Learn:
How multi-tiered supply chains obscure labor exploitation
Why auditing systems fail to catch forced labor
What consumers and corporations can actually do differently

title: When slavery isn't abolished—but outsourced | Bonnie Nixon | TEDxJacksonville
